Aqua by the Bay development changes raise wetland concerns near Sarasota Bay
WWSB ABC7 News at 6pm
By Alyssa Perry
Published: Jul. 30, 2026 at 6:58 PM EDT
Share
Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google
BRADENTON, Fla. ( WWSB ) - Many people are raising concerns about proposed changes to Aqua by the Bay, a 529-acre master-planned community located just west of El Conquistador Parkway near Sarasota Bay.
The development has already received approval, but the developer is now seeking to modify how part of it is built. Those changes could result in the removal of wetlands and the natural buffers surrounding them.
Ryan Gandy, executive director of the Sarasota Bay Estuary, said the area’s fragmented ecosystem makes every remaining wetland critical.
“We have such a fractured ecosystem here with mangroves and wetlands that every little bit that we have right now is highly important,” Gandy said.
Environmental advocates say the wetlands help protect water quality and can reduce flooding during heavy rainfall. Gandy also noted the broader ecological impact.
“If you like going out on the bay and seeing fish and birds and dolphins? They all rely on the productivity of those mangroves,” Gandy said.
Resident Donna Morrison said developer responsiveness to community pushback could shape the outcome.
“If the developers get enough pushbacks willing to make modifications to be able to move forward without you having the whole community fighting them,” Morrison said.
State regulators are accepting public comments on the developer’s request through Aug. 7.
Regulators will review those comments before deciding whether to approve the proposed changes.
The developer did not respond to a request for comment.

Suncoast Aqua Ventures Marks 10 Years of Reef & Beach Cleanup in Terra Ceia
September 4, 2026 | Suncoast Post Staff | Events | No Comments on Suncoast Aqua Ventures Marks 10 Years of Reef & Beach Cleanup in Terra Ceia
For a decade, volunteers with Suncoast Aqua Ventures have been doing something very simple that produces very visible results: getting trash out of the Suncoast’s waterways, shorelines and coastal communities.
That effort continues on Saturday, September 12, 2026, when the nonprofit hosts its 10th Annual Reef & Beach Cleanup at Terra Ceia SeaBreeze Park, 55 Horseshoe Loop Road in Terra Ceia. The event runs from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. and once again combines environmental stewardship with a friendly “Cash for Trash” competition.
Event details are confirmed on the organization’s official website.
Event Information and Registration: 10th Annual Reef and Beach Cleanup registration
Suncoast Aqua Ventures 10th Annual Reef and Beach Cleanup event poster
Turning Trash Into Competition
A Decade of Cleaning Local Waters
Suncoast Aqua Ventures also works alongside organizations with similar environmental missions, including the Sarasota Bay Estuary Program, Keep Manatee Beautiful, Coastal Conservation Association and Sarasota Bay Watch.
A look at upcoming and previous cleanup projects is available on the organization’s events page .
The organization says the Reef & Beach Cleanup alone has removed more than 150,000 pounds of debris during its history. Event organizers report that nearly 390,000 pounds of debris in total have been removed since Suncoast Aqua Ventures was founded in 2016.
Regardless of the accounting discrepancy, hundreds of thousands of pounds of material have been removed through Suncoast Aqua Ventures cleanup efforts during the organization’s decade of work.
More Than a Cleanup
It gives residents an opportunity to personally improve the places where they fish, boat, paddle, dive, swim and spend time with their families.
After 10 years, Suncoast Aqua Ventures is hoping its anniversary cleanup can produce another milestone — and perhaps push its reported lifetime cleanup total beyond 400,000 pounds.
Join the 10th Annual Reef & Beach Cleanup
Date: Saturday, September 12, 2026 Time: 8 a.m. – 6 p.m. Location: SeaBreeze Park, 55 Horseshoe Loop Road, Terra Ceia, FL 34250 Registration: 10th Annual Reef and Beach Cleanup
Follow Suncoast Aqua Ventures for additional cleanup information and event updates through Facebook , Instagram and the organization’s website .
For residents who care about keeping the Suncoast’s land and water free from debris, September 12 offers a chance to get involved — and to help Suncoast Aqua Ventures begin its next decade of cleaning up the community.

Public comment sought for Aqua’s proposed gabion wall
By Joe Hendricks
The proposed gabion wall would be built along the Sarasota Bay shoreline. – Apple Maps | Submitted
MANATEE COUNTY – On July 17, the U.S.
Army Corps of Engineers Jacksonville District issued a public notice regarding an application to construct a gabion wall along the Long Bar Point/Sarasota Bay shoreline as part of the Aqua/ Sea Spray development formerly known as Long Bar Pointe and Aqua by the Bay.
Aqua is located along El Conquistador Parkway in unincorporated Manatee County.
– Joe Hendricks | Sun
The federal agency seeks public comment on the proposed gabion wall and Friday, Aug. 7, is the submission deadline. Public comment can be submitted at the Army Corps website (scroll down to Long Bar Pointe item).
The partially completed, partially occupied, multi-phase development is located along the El Conquistador Parkway in unincorporated Manatee County.
According to Wikipedia, “A gabion wall is a retaining or erosion-control structure made of wire mesh cages (baskets) filled with rock, stone, or other rubble.”
This diagram illustrates the elevations of the proposed gabion wall.
The Army Corps public notice lists Carlos Beruff and Peter Logan as the applicants. The public notice lists Long Bar Pointe LLLP and CARGOR Partners VIII as the applicant companies.
According to the public notice, “The applicant is requesting a DA (Department of the Army) permit to develop a 169.44-acre site in Manatee County, Florida.
To facilitate this development, the applicant seeks authorization to discharge fill material [into] 3.07 acres of wetland systems, which includes 2.76 acres of freshwater wetlands and 0.31 acres of man-made agricultural conveyances.”
Supporting infrastructure includes internal roadways, parking facilities, a dog park and a stormwater management system (wet detention ponds).”
Many Aqua condos and townhomes are now occupied. – Joe Hendricks | Sun
On July 26, Cortez Village Historical Society (CVHS) Vice President Paul Dryfoos sent an email to Suncoast Waterkeeper representatives that said, “We in Cortez are concerned about the Long Bar Pointe application to the Army Corps of Engineers for a development that would entail filling over three acres of wetlands and constructing an 8- to
10-foot-high gabion wall along the waterway boundary. We note that Suncoast Waterkeeper has advocated against this type of encroachment in the past.”
More Aqua homes will be built along the Sarasota Bay shoreline. – Joe Hendricks | Sun
This wetland impacts map was previoujsly provided to the Southwest Florida Water Management District with Aqua’s major modification permit application. – Submitted
